_note: ONE shared file. The pipeline, the backend and the website all read limits from here. Change numbers here, never in code. caution_from/high_from = null means 'trend only' (no US health limit fits this card). Reasons and sources: docs/US_DATA_RESEARCH.md.

hot_days.label: Very hot days
hot_days.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily max temperature T2M_MAX, ~50 km grid
hot_days.day_temp_source: 95 °F, one of the fixed extreme-heat levels (90/95/100/105 °F) used in US Environmental Public Health Tracking
hot_days.cutoff_source: 95 °F is one of the fixed hot-day levels (90, 95, 100, 105 °F) used in US environmental public health tracking; 30 and 60 days (about one and two months a year) are team-defined.

warm_nights.label: Warm nights
warm_nights.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily min temperature T2M_MIN, ~50 km grid
warm_nights.night_temp_source: team-defined: 75 °F; NWS HeatRisk treats unusually warm overnight lows as adding to heat stress
warm_nights.cutoff_source: NWS HeatRisk counts unusually warm overnight lows as adding to heat stress; the 75 °F level and the 30/90-night cutoffs are team-defined to pick out the warmest US night climates.

cold_days.label: Very cold nights
cold_days.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily min temperature T2M_MIN, ~50 km grid
cold_days.cutoff_source: Cold causes more US deaths than heat (JAMA Network Open, 2025), but no US agency sets one cold-night health limit, so 10 °F and the 10/30-night cutoffs are team-defined.

heavy_rain_days.label: Heavy rain days
heavy_rain_days.data: NASA POWER daily precipitation PRECTOTCORR, ~50 km grid
heavy_rain_days.rain_source: official: ETCCDI index R20mm (very heavy precipitation days)
heavy_rain_days.cutoff_source: US agencies define heavy rain against each place's own history (its top 1% of days), not one national count, and a 50 km grid smooths local downpours, so this card shows the trend only.

wettest_day.label: Wettest day of the year
wettest_day.data: NASA POWER daily precipitation PRECTOTCORR, ~50 km grid
wettest_day.rule: maximum daily rain in each year
wettest_day.cutoff_source: US agencies define heavy rain against each place's own history (its top 1% of days), not one national count, and a 50 km grid smooths local downpours, so this card shows the trend only.

dry_days.label: Very dry days
dry_days.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) relative humidity RH2M, ~50 km grid
dry_days.cutoff_source: There is no US health limit for outdoor humidity; NWS fire-weather warnings start near 15% humidity together with strong wind, so this card shows the trend only.

muggy_days.label: Muggy days
muggy_days.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) dew point T2MDEW, ~50 km grid
muggy_days.cutoff_source: Meteorologists call dew points of 70 °F uncomfortable and 75 °F oppressive; 30 and 90 days are team-defined comfort cutoffs, not a health limit.

humid_heat_days.label: Humid-heat days
humid_heat_days.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily-mean wet-bulb temperature T2MWET, ~50 km grid
humid_heat_days.wet_bulb_source: owner decision 2026-11-15 (D27): a daily-mean wet-bulb of 24 °C or more is a humid-heat day (docs/DATA_ADDITIONS.md)
humid_heat_days.cutoff_source: Trend only: there is no US health limit for a yearly count of humid-heat days.

heat_index_days.label: Dangerous heat-index days
heat_index_days.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily max temperature T2M_MAX and dew point T2MDEW, ~50 km grid
heat_index_days.rule: heat index at the day's highest temperature >= heat_index_f
heat_index_days.heat_index_source: official: 103 °F is where the National Weather Service's heat index chart turns from Extreme Caution to Danger (weather.gov/ama/heatindex); heat index by the NWS Rothfusz regression
heat_index_days.cutoff_source: Trend only: the National Weather Service's Danger level is for a single day, not a yearly count.

frost_free_season.label: Frost-free season
frost_free_season.unit: days between last spring and first fall frost
frost_free_season.data: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) daily min temperature T2M_MIN, ~50 km grid
frost_free_season.rule: days from the last spring night at or below frost_c (before July) to the first fall one (from July)
frost_free_season.frost_source: official: 32 °F, the frost-free season definition in the US climate indicators (NOAA Climate.gov; Kunkel)
frost_free_season.unavailable_reason: frost is too rare here to measure a frost-free season
frost_free_season.cutoff_source: Trend only: a longer frost-free season means a longer pollen season and more time for ticks and mosquitoes; there is no health limit for its length.

smoke_days.label: Smoke days
smoke_days.unit: days / year with medium or thick smoke overhead
smoke_days.data: NOAA Hazard Mapping System smoke polygons (drawn by analysts from satellite images), medium and heavy outlines only, on the ~50 km MERRA-2 grid; from 2011. Light outlines are left out: that smoke is often high above the ground, and NOAA changed how it labels smoke density in 2022 (Liu et al. 2024, International Journal of Wildland Fire)
smoke_days.cutoff_source: Trend only: smoke overhead is not always smoke at ground level, so no health limit applies.

aod.label: Haze (aerosol optical depth)
aod.data: NASA MERRA-2 M2TMNXAER total aerosol extinction (TOTEXTTAU, 550 nm), ~50 km grid
aod.cutoff_source: Trend only: optical depth measures haze through the whole air column, not the air people breathe.

rain_sat.label: Rain seen from satellites (IMERG)
rain_sat.data: NASA GPM IMERG Final V07 monthly precipitation, ~10 km grid, to September 2025
rain_sat.cutoff_source: Trend only: a second, satellite-based rain record beside NASA POWER.

surface_heat_5km.label: Summer ground heat (5 km)
surface_heat_5km.data: NASA MODIS MOD11C3 v061 monthly daytime land-surface temperature (Terra), 0.05° grid; trend to 2022 (orbit drift after)
surface_heat_5km.cutoff_source: Trend only: ground temperature is not air temperature; it shows how hot streets and fields get in the sun.

water_storage.label: Water storage (ground, soil, snow)
water_storage.unit: cm of water vs the 2004–2009 average
water_storage.data: NASA/DLR GRACE and GRACE-FO JPL mascons RL06.3 (gravity satellites), ~300 km effective; gap mid-2017 to mid-2018
water_storage.cutoff_source: Trend only: a regional water budget; falling means the area is losing stored water.

pm25.label: Fine particle pollution (PM2.5)
pm25.data: NASA MERRA-2 aerosol diagnostics M2TMNXAER (monthly), PM2.5 rebuilt from dust, sea salt, sulfate, black and organic carbon (no nitrate), ~50 km grid; from 2010, because the model's fire-smoke input changed that year and its PM2.5 jumps in 2009–10 where EPA ground monitors fell (D41)
pm25.caution_source: official: US EPA primary annual standard (2024), upheld by the D.C. Circuit in June 2026
pm25.high_source: official: US EPA secondary annual standard and WHO interim target 3 (15 µg/m³)

no2.label: Traffic & industry pollution (NO₂)
no2.data: NASA OMI/Aura tropospheric NO2 column OMNO2d (daily, 0.25° ≈ 25 km), 2005 onward; the team files' version (003 or 004) is not yet confirmed (D10)
no2.cutoff_source: none: there is no official health limit for satellite NO2 columns, so this card shows the trend only

fires.label: Fire detections nearby
fires.data: NASA FIRMS MODIS active fires (Terra + Aqua, C6.1, 1 km; vegetation type 0, confidence >= 30 = nominal + high); trend from 2003
fires.cutoff_source: A detection is a 1 km satellite pixel with one or more fires, often a farm or prescribed burn, and smoke travels far beyond 50 km, so the count shows nearby fire activity as a trend, not a health level.

surface_heat.label: Neighborhood surface heat
surface_heat.data: NASA MODIS/Terra MOD11A2 v061 (8-day, 1 km, ~10:30 am overpass), via ORNL DAAC; trend 2001-2022 because Terra's orbit drifted after 2020
surface_heat.rule: average daytime land surface temperature in summer (Jun-Aug north, Dec-Feb south), 3 x 3 km around the address
surface_heat.cutoff_source: No health limit exists for ground temperature, and EPA says air temperature, not surface temperature, best reflects what people feel, so this card shows the trend only.

heat_island.label: Heat island vs surroundings
heat_island.rule: summer daytime surface temperature: 3 x 3 km around the address minus the 11 x 11 km area around it
heat_island.cutoff_source: Across 38 US cities, built-up land was on average 4.3 °C hotter at the surface than surrounding land on summer days (NASA MODIS, Imhoff et al. 2010), so +4 °C marks a typical city-scale heat island and +2 °C half of it; both cutoffs are team-defined.

settings.verdict_rule: High risk if any main factor is red · Caution if any is yellow · otherwise Suitable. Trend-only cards (no limit) don't change the verdict.
